 WHAT TO EXPECT: Severe storms, flash flooding possible across Arizona
 Wednesday and Thursday will be ABC15 Weather Action Days as a reminder to stay safe in the storm. 
 Prev 
 Next 
 We are tracking another storm system on the way that will drop temperatures for the rest of the week and bring rain chances back to the Valley. This system is pulling in near-record moisture for this time of year, some of it from the remnants of Trudy south of Baja California. 
 By: 
 Amber Sullins , Jorge Torres , Geneva Zoltek 
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 A powerful fall storm is moving into Arizona.
 Winds will pick up, temperatures will drop and strong to severe storms will impact parts of the state. 
 Wednesday and Thursday will be ABC15 Weather Action Days as a reminder to take action and stay safe in the storms.
 Damaging winds over 60 mph and large hail up to 2 inches in diameter will be possible with some of the strongest storms that move through. 
 Isolated tornadoes are possible too, particularly across parts of the high country on Wednesday. 
 Heavy downpours could lead to flooding in many areas. That's why much of the state is under Flood Watches Wednesday and Thursday. 
 Parts of the Valley could get up to an inch of rain, with 1 to 2 inches in the foothills north and east of Phoenix. Some high country spots could see 2 to 3 inches!
 Valley temperatures will plunge into the 70s by Friday as our forecast starts to dry back out. That will put us around 10 degrees below normal for this time of year.
 We’re back in the 80s over the weekend, and at this point our forecast across most of the state is looking dry.
